title: Fibral criterion for multiplicative type using torsion orders
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $G\to S$ an affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] group scheme of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. A group scheme means an $S$-scheme with multiplication, identity $e:S\to G$ and inverse satisfying the group diagrams. For $s\in S$, put $G_s=G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, where $\kappa(s)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field] and products are fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. For each integer $n>1$, let $G_s[n]$ be the scheme-theoretic inverse image of the identity under the scheme morphism $G_s\to G_s$, $g\mapsto g^n$; no commutativity of $G$ is assumed in defining this scheme.

Suppose that (a) for every $s\in S$ there are an algebraically closed field $\Omega_s$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], a field extension $\kappa(s)\to\Omega_s$ [def-pc-field-extension], a finitely generated additive abelian group $M_s$, and an isomorphism of $\Omega_s$-group schemes $G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_s\simeq D_{\Omega_s}(M_s)$, with the Hopf structure of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]; and (b) for every integer $n>1$, every $G_s[n]$ is finite over $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and the function
$$d_n(s)=\dim_{\kappa(s)}\Gamma(G_s[n],\mathcal O_{G_s[n]})$$
is locally constant on $S$ (each inverse image of an integer is open).

Then $G$ is of multiplicative type: there is an fppf covering $\{U_a\to S\}$ [def-pc-fppf-site] and finitely generated abelian groups $N_a$ such that $G\times_SU_a\simeq D_{U_a}(N_a)$ as $U_a$-group schemes. Here $D_U(N)=\operatorname{Spec}_U\mathcal O_U[N]$ is obtained by gluing the affine group-algebra spectra of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group] over affine opens of $U$. The field $\Omega_s$ in (a) need not be algebraic over $\kappa(s)$; one such algebraically closed extension for each point suffices. There are no Noetherian, reducedness, connectedness, smoothness or residue-characteristic restrictions.

source.place: Theorem B.4.1, printed pp.297-299, sufficiency direction; opening paragraph of B.4, printed p.297, makes the geometric-fibre condition independent of the algebraically closed extension used. Corollary B.4.2(1) uses this criterion on p.300. WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf; read online. No Stacks tag states this group-scheme structural criterion.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$, choose an affine open $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing $s$, and use the geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_s\to S_0$ supplied by (a). The restriction $G_0=G\times_SS_0$ is affine by the definition of an affine morphism. Set $T=(S_0)_{(\bar s)}=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $H=G_0\times_{S_0}T$. Apply [lem-sfb-strict-local-diagonalizable-clopen-lift] to get a finitely generated group $M$ and an open and closed group immersion $j:D_C(M)\to H$ whose closed fibre is an isomorphism. The ring $C$ is local by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure]. Every open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ containing its closed point is the whole spectrum: a principal open containing the maximal ideal is defined by a unit, and principal opens form a basis.

source.place: Theorem B.4.1 proof, p.298: strict-local reduction and the clopen lifting claim; locality from Stacks Tag 04HX (etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring).

proof.text: For $t\in T$ mapping to $x\in S$, formation of the power morphism and its identity inverse image commutes with base change, by the fibre-product universal property. The affine fibre-product formula identifies the coordinate algebra of $H_t[n]$ with that of $G_x[n]$ tensored from $\kappa(x)$ to $\kappa(t)$. A basis of the finite-dimensional former algebra remains a basis after this scalar extension. Consequently its dimension is $d_n(x)$, so the torsion-order function on $T$ is the pullback of $d_n$ and is locally constant. For each $n>1$, the locus where it equals its value at the closed point is open and contains that point; step 1 shows that this locus is all of $T$. This argument is separate for each $n$ and never intersects infinitely many neighbourhoods.

source.place: Theorem B.4.1 proof, p.298, comparison of orders over the connected local base; affine base change is Stacks Tag 01I4, schemes.tex, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes.

proof.text: The group-algebra Hopf formula gives $D_C(M)[n]=D_C(M/nM)$: the power map sends $e_m$ to $e_{nm}$ and the identity fibre imposes $e_{nm}=1$. By the finitely generated abelian group structure theorem, $M/nM$ is finite for $n>1$. Thus every fibre of this torsion scheme has order $|M/nM|$, using its group-algebra basis. Since $j$ is an isomorphism on the closed fibre, this number equals the constant order in step 2. For every $t$, the induced map $j_t[n]$ is a closed immersion, since it is the inverse image of $j_t$ under $H_t[n]\to H_t$; both schemes are finite of the same order. Its coordinate map is therefore a surjection between vector spaces of the same finite dimension, hence an isomorphism. This proves equality of all the torsion subschemes, including nonreduced torsion.

source.place: Theorem B.4.1 proof, p.298, equal-order torsion comparison; explicit group-algebra calculation replaces the torsion-detection reference.

proof.text: Fix $t\in T$, with image $x\in S$. By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields], the extensions $\kappa(t)/\kappa(x)$ and $\Omega_x/\kappa(x)$ embed in a common field; take an algebraic closure $F$ of that field. Hypothesis (a) now identifies $H_t\times_{\kappa(t)}F$ with $D_F(N)$ for some finitely generated $N$. The image $K$ of $j_t$ after this extension is an open and closed subgroup of $D_F(N)$ and contains every $D_F(N)[n]$ by step 3. Here base change of the open inclusion is restriction to the inverse-image open, and base change of the closed inclusion is the same quotient ideal after tensoring. Thus no commutativity of $H$ has been assumed: commutativity is available only in this split geometric fibre.

source.place: Theorem B.4.1 proof, pp.297-298, geometric fibre comparison. Common extensions: Stacks Tag 0H7K, fields.tex, lemma-common-extension-field.

proof.text: By [lem-sbc-finitely-generated-abelian-group-structure], $N\simeq\mathbf Z^r\oplus\bigoplus_i\mathbf Z/a_i\mathbf Z$ with finitely many $a_i\geq1$; apply [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria] to this decomposition to write $D_F(N)=\mathbf G_m^r\times\prod_i\mu_{a_i}$. In characteristic $p>0$, write $a_i=p^{b_i}c_i$ with $(p,c_i)=1$; in characteristic zero put $c_i=a_i$. The connected components of $\mu_{a_i}$ are the one-point thickenings at the $c_i$-th roots of unity, because $z^{a_i}-1=(z^{c_i}-1)^{p^{b_i}}$ in characteristic $p$; the torus factor is connected by the cited criterion. Each component of the product therefore contains the point with torus coordinates $1$ and with these roots of unity as its other coordinates. That point has finite order. Choosing a multiple $n>1$ of its order puts it in $D_F(N)[n]\subset K$. A clopen subset meeting a connected component contains that entire component. Hence $K=D_F(N)$. Field extension is surjective on spectra of finite-type field algebras (a residue-field tensor with a field extension is nonzero, as witnessed by a vector-space basis), so $j_t$ is surjective. This holds for every $t$, so $j$ is surjective; a surjective open immersion is an isomorphism by [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Theorem B.4.1 proof, p.298, concluding that j is an isomorphism; elementary component calculation from the product decomposition (Milne, Algebraic Groups, Proposition 12.3 and Remark 12.5, pp.231-232) supplies the argument.

proof.text: It remains to descend this isomorphism to a pointed etale neighbourhood of $s$, not to treat the strict localization as an fppf cover. Write $G_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The affine finite-presentation criterion makes $B$ finitely presented over $R$. The abelian-group structure theorem gives a presentation $R[M]\simeq R[x_1,y_1,\ldots,x_r,y_r,z_1,\ldots,z_q]/(x_iy_i-1,z_j^{a_j}-1)$ with finitely many generators and relations. By the definition of strict henselization, $C$ is the filtered colimit of affine pointed-etale neighbourhood rings of $S_0$; use [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex] to index it by a directed set, using the base changes of $B$ and $R[M]$ as models at any chosen starting stage. Apply clauses (2) and (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-category-fp-algebras] to the coordinate maps of $j$ and its inverse. They descend to one stage; after advancing that stage their two composites are identities. Advance once more so the multiplication, unit and inverse equations hold. These are finitely many equalities of algebra maps between finitely presented algebras, including the tensor-square algebras, which have the presentations obtained by taking two copies of the generators and relations. Thus for some affine pointed etale neighbourhood $U_s\to S_0$ there is a group isomorphism $G\times_SU_s\simeq D_{U_s}(M)$.

source.place: Theorem B.4.1 proof, pp.297-298, spreading the strict-local isomorphism. Stacks Tags 01TQ (morphisms.tex, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), 0032 (categories.tex, lemma-directed-category-system), and 05N9 (algebra.tex, lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras).

proof.text: Choose such a pointed $U_s$ for each $s\in S$ and compose its map $U_s\to S_0$ with the open inclusion $S_0\hookrightarrow S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], clause (1) the open inclusion is etale and clause (2) the composite $U_s\to S$ is etale. By [def-weil-etale-morphism] each composite is flat and locally of finite presentation, and the images cover $S$ because each $U_s$ has its chosen point above $s$. Hence $\{U_s\to S\}_{s\in S}$ is an fppf covering of $S$ in the sense of [def-pc-fppf-site]. The isomorphisms of step 6 are exactly those required by the conclusion. If $S$ is empty, the empty family is jointly surjective and gives the conclusion directly.
